title: FULLY RETRACTABLE SOLAR ARRAYS FOR MISSIONS TO SATURN EXPRO+
description: ObjectivesTo develop a solar array design for use in deep space missions to Saturn.DescriptionFor an orbiting satellite to pass safely through the rings of Saturn, the solar array needs tobe retractable. In order to minimize target area, the array should alsobe fully flexible. Fullyretractable and flexible arrays are currently being developed for telecommunicationmissions, which may form the starting point of this development. With a high specificpower, such arrays lend themselves for use in exploration missions.Recent feasibility studies have demonstrated that missions to Saturn, fully powered bysolar arrays, are indeed feasible. However, the total area needed would be between 150 -200 m2. This places demanding requirements on the solar array design. Apart from highspecific power (W/kg) and low areal mass (kg/m2), other important parameters include theeigenfrequencies in stowed and deployed configurations, as well as the ability to retractand to re-deploy, to protect the array from damage, should the satellite pass through thedust rings of Saturn.The activity therefore encompasses the following tasks:Design of a solar array with a cell area of 100 m2.- Development of deployment mechanisms to allow array retraction.- Assessment of areal mass, using latest LILT solar cell technology, potentially modified with reduced thickness.- Assessment of eigenfrequencies for arrays of up to 100 m2 area.- Demonstration ofmultiple retractions and re-deployments of the solar array by means oftest at low temperature of a representative design mock-up.- Identification of development needs.- Preparation of a roadmap.

title: ExoMars - Rosalind Franklin Mission (EXM-RFM): Invitation to Tender for Isolation Valves
description: The Rosalind Franklin Mission represents the continuation of ESA’s ExoMars programme following the breakup of the inter-Agency agreement with Roscosmos. As such, it replaces the previous Rover & Surface Platform Mission. The main objectives of the Rosalind Franklin Mission are to safely land on the Mars surface, collect and analyse in situ a range of Martian surface and subsurface soil samples, and to demonstrate technologies for planetary exploration. The key elements of the ‘Rosalind Franklin’ Rover are its advanced drilling system, coupled with a sophisticated on-board science laboratory, and its capability to move autonomously on a variety of terrains on Mars’ surface for at least 218 sols (8 months). Sampling down to a depth of 2 metres significantly increases the probability to detect preserved signs of past or even present life. The analysis of soil geo-chemistry will provide a detailed characterisation of the environment and geological history, and possibly provide evidence for the presence of organic compounds. The ‘Rosalind Franklin’ Rover will be placed on the surface of Mars by an Entry, Descent and Landing Module (EDLM). This module is the main new developmental element of the ExoMars-Rosalind Franklin mission and will require key contributions from European suppliers. The so-called “braking engines” will be provided by NASA as Customer Furnished Items (CFIs). The Rover System comprises the ‘Rosalind Franklin’ Rover Module and the Rover Operations Control Centre (ROCC), the latter developed by and located at ALTEC in Torino (Italy), where the ground operations of the Rover surface mission will be performed. The Rover and its payload will require maintenance and some upgrades to manage obsolescence and ensure compliance with the new mission requirements associated with the 2028 launch scenario. The ‘Rosalind Franklin’ Rover will benefit from the provision by NASA of Radio-Isotope Heating Units (RHUs). These RHUs are required to support the thermal control system of the Rover, replacing similar units previously provided by Roscosmos. The new flight system also requires the maintenance of the existing Carrier Module and of the Descent Module equipment and subsystems already developed by ESA. The launch services (launcher and launch site facilities) will also be provided by NASA. Airbus Defence and Space Ltd is the Lead Contractor for the Landing Platform Mechanical Thermal and Propulsion System (“MTPS”). As part of their scope of work, Airbus will release an Invitation to Tender (ITT) looking for a supplier of the Propulsion Isolation Valves. The Landing Platform will require at least 6 Propulsion Isolation Valves which will be used on the propulsion system.

Jos saman tarjoajan henkilöstö olisi valittavissa usean osa-alueen toteuttajaksi, henkilöstö kohdennetaan tarjoajan ilmoittaman etusijajärjestyksen mukaisesti korkeimmalle sijoittamalleen osa-alueelle. Muiden osa-alueiden osalta siirrytään kyseisen osa-alueen paremmuusjärjestyksessä seuraavaan kelvolliseen rinnakkaistarjoukseen, jonka henkilöstö ei ole päällekkäinen jo valitun henkilöstön kanssa. Menettelyä jatketaan, kunnes kullekin osa-alueelle on löydetty valittavissa oleva tarjous tai kaikki kyseisen osa-alueen rinnakkaistarjoukset on käyty läpi. Jos kaksi tai useampi tarjoaja saa samasta osa-alueesta saman lopullisen vertailupistemäärän, etusijalle asetetaan tarjoaja, jonka laadun vertailupisteet ovat korkeammat. Jos myös laadun vertailupisteet ovat samat, tarjoajien keskinäinen järjestys ratkaistaan arpomalla.
